reasoning: The question asks if Tesla will have driverless ride-hailing in the US by end of year (2025). Evidence shows Tesla launched robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025 with human safety supervisors initially, then claimed to begin testing without human monitors in early December. However, multiple sources indicate: (1) only ~31-72 active vehicles in Austin as of late 2025, (2) San Francisco service uses human drivers, not driverless, (3) Musk's repeated promises for 500 robotaxis in Austin by year-end were revised down to ~60, (4) no permits for driverless operation in California, (5) the resolution criteria require 10,000 bona fide driverless rides with no observers, >400m distance, by year-end. Evidence of actual driverless rides is minimal—one source mentions 112 rides early in launch with teleoperators monitoring. The gap between Musk's claims and actual driverless operations is substantial. Given the strict resolution criteria (10,000 rides, no human backup, no observers, >400m distance) and evidence of only limited driverless testing rather than systematic commercial operation, reaching 10,000 qualifying rides by year-end appears highly unlikely.
